transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

You likely need a new heating element, as this is the most common cause of a tumble dryer running without heat. However, it could also be a faulty thermal fuse or thermostat if those components have failed. From what you have described, the most likely cause is heater element. Some programmes (cool air, refresh, delicates or a low-heat option) dry with little or no heat. Was a cool-air or low-heat programme set (and have you changed it), or was it a normal heat programme?
Normal heat programme, and I tried both high and low heat on the dial - cold on both. So which part do I need?

It depends on whether the heating element or the thermal fuse is faulty, as either could cause cold air output. You would need to replace whichever specific component fails a continuity test. A blocked lint filter stops the airflow, and many dryers then cut the heat to stop overheating. Clean the fluff filter in the door opening (heat-pump models often have a second one at the bottom too). Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

The lint filter was fairly full, I've cleaned it now. Also the vent hose had a big sag full of fluff, which I cleaned out. Still cold after 20 min though. I can't test continuity, no multimeter. So which part?

It depends on whether the heating element is actually receiving power, as a faulty thermostat or thermal fuse could also cut off heat. Without testing components with a multimeter, you cannot definitively identify the specific failed part. Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

Mine's a vented one with the hose out the window, so I don't think it has a condenser or second filter. The hose was really clogged with fluff before it died, if that matters. Is it the thermal fuse or the element then, and what's the part number?

[Heading: Likely cause: heater element]
I cannot provide specific part numbers as I do not have your exact model details. The fault could be the heating element, thermostat, or thermal cut-out, but identifying the correct component requires knowing the precise model number. From what you have checked, this points to the heater element. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door opening.
[Safety panel] Clean the lint filter after every load — a build-up of fluff is a fire risk and restricts airflow. Don't run the dryer overnight or while you're out.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It says DV7110 on the front but I can't get at the label on the back, the dryer's wedged in a tight alcove against the wall. Is DV7110 enough to go on for the part?

[Heading: Likely cause: heater element]
No, the model number DV7110 is not sufficient because it only identifies the machine type, not the specific component. You need the full alphanumeric code printed on the label of the actual part you intend to replace. The checks point to the heater element. I could not find a confirmed match for model DV7110 in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
